diagnosis: The scenario failed the Weak Arm gate because all rollouts resulted in decisions that align with default/public information rather than the hidden facts. Specifically, the models consistently chose 'diploma release for all graduating seniors' (ignoring PF1), 'one ceremony session' and 'three guest tickets' (ignoring PF2), 'English-only announcements' (ignoring PF3), and 'general seating' (ignoring PF4). No checks passed, meaning the model was able to make a complete decision without needing any of the private information provided by agents A2, A3, A4, or A5.

fix_instructions: To ensure the scenario requires multi-agent coordination, tighten the content checks so they cannot be satisfied by default values or common sense. For example: tighten C3 and C6 (dependent on PF1) to require a specific count of seven withheld diplomas; tighten C1, C2, and C7 (dependent on PF2) to strictly enforce the two-session limit and the two-guest ticket maximum; tighten C4 and C8 (dependent on PF3) to explicitly require the inclusion of Spanish and Somali interpretation; and tighten C5, C9, and P1 (dependent on PF4) to mandate separate entrances and cite the counselor's safety fact.
